newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco ministers told to step down before poll.
newsitem.headline: Morocco ministers told to step down before poll.

text.p: Moroccan King Hassan has told more than a dozen government ministers they should step down to focus on campaigning for the general election to be held later this year.

The official news agency MAP said the king told members of the government who belonged to political parties that he preferred they do this, although under the constitution they could remain in office.

MAP said that "despite the constitution allowing them to remain in government while leading electoral campaigns, His Majesty judged it preferable from a moral viewpoint that...they should devote themselves entirely to their political and partisan activity".

The king's statement was seen as presaging a reshuffle of the government, headed by Prime Minister Abdellatif Filali, who has no party affiliation. Filali is also foreign minister and has held his posts since November 1993.
Several others including Interior Minister Driss Basri also have no party ties and would be expected to remain.
A statement carried on MAP said the cabinet, chaired by the king, approved a decree convening a special meeting of parliament for August 17.

Parliamentary elections were expected to be held late in September, a year after a referendum overwhelmingly approved introduction of a two-house parliament instead of the existing single-house system. Newspapers have suggested that the ballot might be put off until late in the year.
The council of ministers met at the royal palace of Skhirat, 20 km (12 miles) south of Rabat, MAP said, adding that the king thanked ministers for their work.
